title: In Proverbs 27 What Does It Mean To Sharpen One Another In Friendship
paragraphs: Iron Sharpens Iron: The Power of Godly Friendship in Proverbs 27
Friendship is a recurring theme in the wisdom literature of the Bible, and few verses capture its profound value quite like Proverbs 27:17:
Iron sharpeneth iron; So a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend. - Proverbs 27:17 ASV

This simple yet vivid proverb uses the imagery of two pieces of iron striking together to produce a sharper edge, illustrating how relationships can bring out the best in us. But what does it truly mean to "sharpen" one another in friendship, especially from a biblical perspective?
The Context of Proverbs 27

Proverbs 27 is filled with practical advice on relationships, humility, and personal growth. Verse 17 sits among other sayings that stress the importance of honest counsel, loyalty, and wisdom in our interactions:
Faithful are the wounds of a friend; But the kisses of an enemy are profuse. - Proverbs 27:6 ASV
These verses together highlight that true friends do not simply flatter; they challenge, correct, and encourage each other toward godliness and wisdom.
What Does "Sharpening" Mean?

The act of sharpening involves friction—sometimes even sparks. Spiritually, sharpening refers to the process of building one another up in the faith, encouraging growth, and holding each other accountable. This is not always comfortable, but it is necessary for spiritual maturity. In the New Testament, this principle is echoed:
Let us consider one another to provoke unto love and good works; not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting one another... - Hebrews 10:24-25 ASV
Sharpening involves:
Encouragement – Lifting each other up when weary or discouraged (1 Thessalonians 5:11).
Accountability – Gently confronting sin and speaking truth in love (Galatians 6:1).
Growth – Challenging each other to pursue Christ and mature in faith (Colossians 1:28).
The Centrality of Christ in Friendship

Christ-centered friendship is not about making each other comfortable, but about spurring one another on to Christlikeness. Jesus Himself modeled this with His disciples, teaching, correcting, and loving them deeply. True friendship seeks the highest good of the other, which is conformity to Christ:
This is my commandment, that ye love one another, even as I have loved you. Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends. - John 15:12-13 ASV
Practical Application: How Can We Sharpen Each Other?
Consider these practical ways to "sharpen" your friends in a godly manner:
Regularly pray for and with your friends (James 5:16).
Be honest and willing to both give and receive constructive feedback (Ephesians 4:15).
Encourage your friends to pursue spiritual disciplines like reading Scripture and serving others.
Walk through trials together, reminding one another of God’s faithfulness (Galatians 6:2).
Biblical Friendship Is a Gift

True, sharpening friendship is a gift from God, designed to help us grow in wisdom and Christlikeness. It is rooted in love, honesty, and mutual pursuit of God’s truth. As believers, we are called to seek out and cultivate these kinds of relationships for our good and God’s glory.
